patch.value: Make the id-resolution prefix test re-roll its setup instead of asserting on a random precondition

test/id-resolution.test.ts could fail in its own setup rather than in the code under test. It created three items, then asserted that uniqueNonExactPrefix(c, [a,b,c]) returned a prefix. Ids are pm- plus four random base36 characters, so the longest usable proper prefix carries only three of them, and whenever another id shares all three the helper correctly returns null and the assertion failed the build. Measured at roughly 6.4e-5 per run, confirmed by simulation at 16 failures in 400000 trials, and observed for real on CI run 30797275564 where test(26) failed while test(22) passed on the same commit whose only change was a lockfile refresh. A setup precondition that depends on chance must be re-rolled, not asserted. Replaced with a bounded retry that rebuilds the chain in a fresh workspace until the newest id has a unique proper prefix, discarding the losing workspace each time so the tracker does not accumulate ids and make a collision more likely.

The prefix precondition is obtained by bounded retry rather than assertion; each failed attempt discards its workspace so retries do not raise collision probability; the bound is documented with the resulting failure probability; the give-up path throws a diagnostic naming the ids; the full suite passes and typecheck is clean.

value.text:
PROBABILITY CORRECTION (raised in review by CodeRabbit, P2).

This item's description states the per-run setup failure probability as 6.4e-5. That figure is WRONG and is superseded by this note.

6.4e-5 counts all THREE id pairs (3 x 36^-3). But the assertion only fails when the SELECTED TARGET's prefix is ambiguous, and a pair between the two non-target ids cannot make the target ambiguous. Only the two pairs involving the target count:

  1 - (1 - 36^-3)^2 = 4.29e-5

The issue's own simulation already agreed with the corrected model and not the original one: 16 failures in 400,000 trials is 4.0e-5, which matches the two-pair figure of 4.29e-5, not the three-pair figure of 6.4e-5. The empirical evidence was in the issue from the start and was read against the wrong model.

Consequences for the implemented fix: none. The bound of 8 attempts was chosen with margin, and at the corrected probability exhaustion is below 1.2e-35 rather than the 1e-33 originally documented, so the fix is if anything safer than claimed. The source comment in test/id-resolution.test.ts now carries the corrected figure.

Not rewriting the earlier history entries: the history ledger is append-only and audited, so a superseded figure is corrected by appending this note rather than by editing the record that stated it.

patch.value: test/id-resolution.test.ts could fail in its own setup rather than in the code under test. Two tests did this: the path test asserted uniqueNonExactPrefix(c, [a,b,c]) and the impact test asserted uniqueNonExactPrefix(a, [a,b,c]). Ids are pm- plus four random base36 characters, so the longest usable proper prefix carries only three of them, and whenever one of the other two ids shares all three the helper correctly returns null and the assertion failed the build. The per-run probability is 1 - (1 - 36^-3)^2, about 4.29e-5, counting only the two pairs that involve the selected target; this matches the observed simulation of 16 failures in 400000 trials. Observed for real on CI run 30797275564 where test(26) failed while test(22) passed on the same commit whose only change was a lockfile refresh. A setup precondition that depends on chance must be re-rolled, not asserted. Replaced with one shared bounded-retry chain builder, parameterised by which end of the chain must be prefix-addressable, that rebuilds in a fresh workspace until the target has a unique proper prefix, discarding the workspace after both a losing roll and a throwing setup so no temporary tracker leaks.

Both flaky setups replaced with one shared bounded-retry chain builder; workspace leak on the throw path closed; probability corrected to 4.29e-5 in code and tracker. PR #54 merged with all checks green, 195/195 tests, and two bot rounds resolved.
